A9-01 Experimental Signatures & Future Tests

The  framework's experimental signatures are not a menu of optional predictions but the necessary consequences of three irreducible constraints: proper time quantization (τ = nℏκ), prime-indexed winding (winding number = prime pₙ), and holographic boundary closure (the worldline must close on itself at the cosmological horizon). The constraint set — one electron, one prime, one worldline — is the unique fixed point from which every experimental signature in this paper falls out as an inevitable shadow. To ask "why this signature?" is to misunderstand the architecture: the constraint is the signature, seen from a particular experimental angle.

The  framework's gap correlation functions Cₙ = ⟨dₖdₖ₊ₙ⟩ generate the QED loop coefficients for g-2, the hadronic vacuum polarization from gap triplets, the electroweak contribution from gap quadruplets, and the new physics signal from gap excess beyond the Standard Model — all from the same gap statistics. A9-14 FCNC Searches

The flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) rates are not parameters to be bounded — they are the necessary consequences of gap topology constraints on flavor transitions. In the  framework, flavor is a gap excitation mode; FCNC processes are forbidden at tree level by the gap topology (no flavor-changing neutral gaps) and arise only from gap correlation loops. The constraint of proper time quantization (τ = nℏκ) forces the worldline to wind through prime-indexed cycles; flavor transitions require gap correlation loops. The constraint of holographic boundary closure forces the loop amplitudes to be finite and quantized. The constraint of prime-indexed winding selects the FCNC rates from the gap correlation functions at specific winding numbers. These three constraints admit no freedom for the FCNC rates. They do not "predict" branching ratios; they exhaust the space of non-contradiction for flavor-changing neutral transitions. The resulting formulas — B → Kγ, B → Kℓ⁺ℓ⁻, B_s → μ⁺μ⁻, K⁺ → π⁺νν̄, μ → eγ, τ → μγ — are not model fits — they are the unique fixed point of the constraint system. The LHCb, Belle II, NA62, MEG, Mu3e limits and future sensitivities — all are inevitable projections of the same gap correlation loops onto different flavor channels. The constraint is* the FCNC rate, seen through the experimental lens of rare decay searches.
The apparent complexity of FCNC physics — effective Hamiltonians (C₇, C₉, C₁₀), form factors, long-distance contributions, new physics contributions (SUSY, Z', leptoquarks, extra dimensions), CP violation in FCNC, angular analyses, isospin asymmetries — resolves into a single structure when viewed through the Williams lens. The CP violation is the gap phase in the loops. The angular analyses are the gap correlation angular distributions. The complexity collapses because the constraint set is minimal: proper time quantization + flavor winding + boundary unitarity. The FCNC rate is not an effective field theory calculation — it is the gap correlation loop amplitude, and the experiments measure the gap correlations directly.

The SM rates must match the electroweak gap correlation loops. The BSM rates must match the BSM gap correlation loops. The B → Kγ, B → Kℓ⁺ℓ⁻, B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ must constrain the gap correlation loops at b-quark winding. The K⁺ → π⁺νν̄ must constrain the gap correlation loops at s-quark winding.
